title: GPU arbiter slab harmonize and KV-sweep incident response
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Customer escalations from three large accounts (hosted + dedicated clusters) surfaced a correlated class of GPU OOMs during sustained long-context inference. Failures manifested as sudden slab saturation inside the allocator coupled with an explosion of stale KV cache tombstones that prevented normal compaction. This ticket coordinates triage, an urgent runtime hotfix, canary rollout, customer comms, and a short-term mitigation for private/VPC customers who cannot receive immediate binary updates.
steps_taken:
2026-02-18: Initial SE alarm from Customer A; collected core dumps, heap profiles, and kv-index snapshots.
2026-02-18: Reproduced under load locally with synthetic long-prefix workload; observed slab growth with slow-to-free arenas and a necked compaction path.
2026-02-19: Isolated two contributors: (1) allocator's slab split heuristic failed under high prefix churn producing many small live slabs; (2) KV cache index left tombstones when concurrent session handoffs coincided with eviction storms.
2026-02-19: Implemented three-part tactical patch in a feature branch (allocator: slab-harmonizer, kvcache: tombstone-sweeper trigger, arbiter: preemptive-evict watermark).
2026-02-20: Unit + integration tests run; synthetic OOM replay shows >90% reduction in peak GPU memory and stable compaction latency.
2026-02-21: Canary rollout to dedicated-us-east-2 region (5% traffic). Monitored 72h: no OOM recurrences; CPU overhead +2.7% steady-state.
2026-02-22: Preparing PR for runtime-2.7.4 and customer patch notes; coordination with Private deployments team for offline patch guidance.
root_cause: Two interacting defects: allocator slab-splitting heuristic creates many small arenas under sustained long-context, high-churn sessions (amplifies fragmentation). Concurrently, the KV cache's lockless eviction path could leave tombstones when a session handoff occurred during aggressive eviction, preventing downstream compaction and causing the allocator to retain many otherwise-reclaimable objects. Under heavy load this produced a rapid, non-linear increase in GPU resident memory culminating in OOMs.
resolution: Applied coordinated runtime fixes: (A) slab-harmonizer - a background migrator that consolidates underutilized small slabs into larger arenas during low-util windows; (B) tombstone-sweeper - a safe, epoch-based compaction pass that reclaims KV index entries once session-affinity barriers are observed; (C) arbiter preemptive-evict watermark - throttles new long-context sessions when memory pressure crosses warning thresholds to give compaction breathing room. The patch set is in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3291 and merged into release branch for runtime-2.7.4.
rollback_plan:
If canary shows regressions beyond acceptable thresholds (OOM recurrence or >10% latency tail regressions):
- Immediately revert runtime-2.7.4 canary deployment via orchestrator (standard rollback job).
- Re-enable graceful-fallback policy to pinned model-variants for affected customers.
- If needed, apply emergency evict-only hotpatch (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3299) that disables slab-harmonizer migration behavior and forces immediate aggressive kvcache GC while preserving tenant isolation.
tests:
- Unit tests for allocator and kv-index compaction added (coverage +6%).
- Stress harness: 48h long-context high-churn replay with 120 concurrent sessions showed zero OOMs vs baseline 6 OOMs/hour.
- Canary observability: token-level memory, GPU resident histograms, KV tombstone counts, compaction latency traces (slo: compaction <500ms p99).
- Private deployment test: offline binary applied to on-prem lab (replicated customer workload) with success criteria validated by Solutions Eng.
